_about: The hand-kept half of the site's Rust tracker (site/rust/). rust/tools/progress.py adds the counted half and writes site/rust/progress.json. Status is one of: done, live, active, next, parked, later.
goal: games against the AI that cost a fraction of the server's CPU: one-on-one games against the AI with Pioneer and Standard decks, decided in milliseconds.

phases.name: Contracts and measurement
phases.text: State traces and fingerprints, decision logs, the wire conformance suite and the AI speed bench. A seeded game replays to the same trace twice in a row.

phases.name: Rust gateway
phases.text: playmat-gateway sits in front of the Java server and routes each group of calls to Java, Rust, or both to compare. It has carried every connection on the public server since 4 Nov 2026.

phases.name: Platform services
phases.text: Card search, deck checks, deck sync, deck import by link, staff records and support in Rust, each answered alongside Java and compared.

phases.name: Career economy
phases.text: Unparked 11 Nov 2026. The Career's records, quests, rerolls, the capsule shop and pulls are in Rust, and payouts run off an outbox Java writes: Rust pays duels and every game outside Career tables, Rust-hosted ones included. Quests and pulls roll the same seeded dice on both sides. Next: two weeks of identical payouts in shadow.

phases.name: Rules engine and card pipeline
phases.text: A Rust rules engine with cheap copies, and a transpiler that turns XMage's Java card files into data. Every card is checked against Java with shadow games. The first pool is in: all 42 Pioneer and Standard school decks and the 24 meta decks the AI plays, plus the Modern meta decks and the starter decks. Gate run (11–12 Nov): 9,949 of 10,000 shadow games match and Java didn't finish 45. The 6 that differ are Java bugs Rust doesn't copy (#289), accepted as such on 12 Nov. 51 of 65 exported card tests pass and none differ; the other 14 can't run outside Java. The pool now covers Pioneer: 7,276 cards are in the engine, and 5,141 are verified (13 Nov), each by three or more matching shadow games that played it. Only verified cards reach Rust games. Next: the rest of the Pioneer pool.

phases.name: Rust AI
phases.text: Whole-turn playouts on engine copies, deciding in milliseconds. It plays the AI's seat in Java's games for listed players, and the whole game when the Rust engine hosts it. Any decider answers through one decision interface (playouts by default; MCTS on parallel threads is opt-in: as strong, far more CPU), and Archbench rates them on fixed seeded duels.

phases.name: Retire Java
phases.text: Started with AI games: since 11 Nov a one-on-one game against the AI can run on the Rust engine with no Java game behind it, for players who turn it on in Settings. Also built: one-on-one tables between people (best-of-three, timers, spectators), and the solo tools on hosted games (saves, "Try this turn again", advice, practice tools). Tournaments and drafts come once the pool covers limited card pools.

steps.name: Measure
steps.text: The server logs what each Rust AI game costs: Java's game thread, the trace, and the Rust copy.
steps.gate: A week of production cost lines

steps.name: Fidelity
steps.text: Every card of the 24 Pioneer and Standard meta decks in the engine, with a shadow game for each pairing: 287 of 288 match, and Java didn't finish the other.
steps.gate: A week of production AI games that follow Java to the end

steps.name: Views in Rust
steps.text: What the client sees (views, prompts and the game log) built by the Rust engine and compared with Java's.
steps.gate: Zero view differences on a week of real games

steps.name: Human side and host
steps.text: A Rust host for the whole game: skip settings, priority timers, mulligans, concede, reconnect, best-of-three, spectators, replays and the Career's pay.
steps.gate: The live client tests pass against a Rust-hosted game

steps.name: Rollout
steps.text: Rust-hosted games for listed players, and for every player who turns on "Play on the Rust engine" in Settings, live since 11 Nov 2026. Then every AI duel whose decks qualify, by default.
steps.gate: A week with no game lost to the host, then the default

steps.name: Then
steps.text: More of the Pioneer pool, and what still plays on Java only: the Career's games and assists, tournaments and drafts. The solo tools, advice, practice tools and games between people are built (phase 6).

measures.label: CPU per AI search node
measures.note: 84 seeded duels with the Pioneer and Standard school decks, one thread. The Rust AI searches fewer nodes per decision, so the decision times are the fairer comparison.

measures.label: AI games won against a random seat, of 48
measures.note: RustAiGameTest: the school decks against a RandomDriver seat, 20-turn cap. Java also drew 9 and lost 2; the Rust AI drew 6 and lost 1.

measures.label: A whole game replayed by the Rust engine
CPU per AI game, hosted on the Rust engine
measures.note: Java: an AI game with Java's AI (8.6 to 12 s). Rust: 12 production games replayed with host-replay (median 0.53 s, worst 0.90 s), about 0.06 s of it process start and loading the cards. The gateway's share isn't in it.

cost.note: CPU seconds per AI game with real decks. Java alone: its own AI. With the Rust AI: the AI's thinking moves to the Rust copy, and what's left is Java hosting the game. Rust hosting (11 Nov): the whole game on the Rust engine, 12 production games replayed with host-replay, user+sys CPU, process start included.

gate.note: the other 6 are Java bugs, 45 more Java didn't finish
